To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the macrostructure of a text is the gist or summary of that text; (2) the macrostructure is generated by a set of macrooperators, which are the inverse of the macrooperators of comprehension; (3) the macrostructure can be generated by a single macrooperator if the text has a simple structure; (4) the macrostructure must be generated by a sequence of macrooperators if the text has complex structure; and (5) a schema controls the macrooperators of generation
(1) text comprehension is the result of a process that is both reproductive and constructive, and (2) text production is the result of the inverse process.

the semantic structure of texts has a microlevel and a macrolevel, that comprehension involves a cyclical microprocess and a macroprocess, that the macroprocess is controlled by a control schema, that the control schema can often be made explicit by asking the comprehender to summarize, and that the macroprocesses can be reversed on production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and empirical evaluation of a model of comprehension and production that is based on the idea that texts have a coherent macrostructure.
